restated_task: Implement the function to_roman(n) in the roman.core module to convert an integer n (1..3999 inclusive) to its standard Roman numeral string using subtractive notation (e.g., 4='IV', 9='IX', 40='XL', 90='XC', 400='CD', 900='CM'). The function must return a str. It must raise ValueError for integer inputs outside the range 1..3999, and raise TypeError for non-integer inputs (including bool, float, str, None, list, etc.). The existing is_roman_numeral function and the test suite must remain unchanged.

interface_contract.name: to_roman
interface_contract.behavior: Converts an integer n in the range 1 to 3999 inclusive to its Roman numeral representation using standard subtractive notation. Returns the Roman numeral as a string (uppercase letters).
error_cases: ValueError: raised when n is an int but not in the range 1..3999 (e.g., 0, -1, 4000).
TypeError: raised when n is not an int (e.g., '5', 5.0, None, [1], True, False).

acceptance_criteria: 11. to_roman returns a value of type str for all valid inputs.
12. to_roman raises ValueError for integer inputs 0, -1, and 4000 (and any other int outside 1..3999).
13. to_roman raises TypeError for non-int inputs: string '5', float 5.0, None, list [1] (and any other non-int type).
out_of_scope: Do not modify the existing is_roman_numeral function.
Do not modify the test files (tests/test_basic.py and tests/__init__.py).
Do not change the public interface of the roman package (i.e., the import structure in roman/__init__.py).
